quote: Lines of text SHOULD NOT be longer than 75 octets, excluding the line break.
test: Generating a SUMMARY of 200 ASCII chars yields physical lines of at most 75 octets (excluding CRLF), each continuation starting with one space.

quote: Long content lines SHOULD be split into a multiple line representations using a line "folding" technique.
test: Any generated content line longer than 75 octets is folded as CRLF + single space; unfolding the output restores the original line byte for byte.

quote: a long line can be split between any two characters by inserting a CRLF immediately followed by a single linear white-space character (i.e., SPACE or HTAB).
test: The parser accepts folds introduced by CRLF+SPACE and by CRLF+HTAB; the generator always emits CRLF+SPACE.

quote: Unfolding is accomplished by removing the CRLF and the linear white-space character that immediately follows.
test:
"DESCRIPTION:ab
 cd
	ef" parses to "abcdef" and "X:a
  b" parses to "a b" (only one whitespace character removed).

quote: When parsing a content line, folded lines MUST first be unfolded according to the unfolding procedure described above.
test: A property whose name is split across a fold (e.g. "DTSTA\r\n RT:20240101T100000Z") is recognised as DTSTART with the correct value.

quote: implementations need to unfold lines in such a way to properly restore the original sequence.
test: A 3-byte character (E2 82 AC) split across a fold by a naive producer decodes to U+20AC because unfolding is done on bytes before UTF-8 decoding; the generator never splits inside a multi-octet sequence (RFC 5545 states no MUST NOT, so this is generator policy).

quote: improperly folded lines in the middle of a UTF-8 multi-octet sequence.
test: A SUMMARY of 25 four-byte emoji is folded with no physical line over 75 octets and no split inside a character, and round-trips identically.

quote: Content lines are delimited by a line break, which is a CRLF sequence (CR character followed by LF character).
test: Generated output uses CRLF after every content line including the last one (no bare LF).

quote: Content lines are delimited by a line break, which is a CRLF sequence (CR character followed by LF character).
test: Leniency policy (not required by the RFC): a file with bare LF line endings parses to the same components as the CRLF version.

quote: All names of properties, property parameters, enumerated property values and property parameter values are case-insensitive.
test: "dtstart;tzid=Europe/Berlin:20240101T100000" and "DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240101T100000" parse identically; "PARTSTAT=accepted" equals ACCEPTED.

quote: Values in a list of values MUST be separated by a COMMA character.
test: "RDATE;VALUE=DATE:19970304,19970504" parses to two dates; the generator joins multiple EXDATE/RDATE values with a comma.

quote: These structured property values MUST have their value parts separated by a SEMICOLON character.
test: An RRULE value "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO" is split on ';' into two parts; the generator joins RECUR parts with ';' never ','.

quote: Each property parameter in a list of property parameters MUST be separated by a SEMICOLON character.
test: "ATTENDEE;ROLE=CHAIR;PARTSTAT=ACCEPTED:mailto:a@x" parses with two parameters and is regenerated with ';' between them.

quote: Property parameters with values containing a COLON character, a SEMICOLON character or a COMMA character MUST be placed in quoted text.
test: CN="Doe, John" is emitted quoted; the parser reads ';CN="a:b;c,d":mailto:x' as parameter value "a:b;c,d" and treats the first unquoted colon as the start of the value.

quote: Property parameter values that contain the COLON, SEMICOLON, or COMMA character separators MUST be specified as quoted-string text values.
test: Setting an attendee CN of "Smith; Jr" generates CN="Smith; Jr" (quoted) while CN=Alice is left unquoted.

quote: Property parameter values MUST NOT contain the DQUOTE character.
test: A CN containing a double quote (Al "Bob") is rejected by the validator (or the quotes are stripped); no generated parameter value contains DQUOTE inside its quoted-string.

quote: Applications MUST ignore x-param and iana-param values they don't recognize.
test: "DTSTART;X-FOO=1:20240101T100000Z" parses without error; when the event is edited the unknown parameter is preserved on rewrite.

quote: The URI parameter value MUST be specified in a quoted-string.
test: DESCRIPTION;ALTREP="cid:p@x":text parses and is regenerated with the ALTREP URI quoted.

quote: If not specified on a property that allows this parameter, the default is INDIVIDUAL.
test: An ATTENDEE without CUTYPE is reported with cutype INDIVIDUAL; an unknown CUTYPE value is treated as UNKNOWN.

quote: The individual calendar address parameter values MUST each be specified in a quoted-string.
test: DELEGATED-TO="mailto:a@x","mailto:b@x" parses into a 2-element list and round-trips with each address quoted and a comma between them.

quote: If the value type parameter is ";VALUE=BINARY", then the inline encoding parameter MUST be specified with the value ";ENCODING=BASE64".
test: ATTACH;VALUE=BINARY;ENCODING=BASE64:aGk= is accepted; ATTACH;VALUE=BINARY:aGk= (no ENCODING) is reported as an error.

quote: The default encoding is "8BIT", corresponding to a property value consisting of text.
test: A property without ENCODING is read as plain text, not base64-decoded.

quote: The values MUST match one of the values allowed for the given calendar component.
test: In a VEVENT ATTENDEE, NEEDS-ACTION/ACCEPTED/DECLINED/TENTATIVE/DELEGATED are accepted; the VTODO-only values COMPLETED and IN-PROCESS are rejected by the generator.

quote: If not specified on a property that allows this parameter, the default value is NEEDS-ACTION.
test: An ATTENDEE without PARTSTAT is reported with partstat NEEDS-ACTION.

quote: Applications MUST treat x-name and iana-token values they don't recognize the same way as they would the NEEDS-ACTION value.
test: ATTENDEE;PARTSTAT=X-FOO:mailto:a@x is interpreted as NEEDS-ACTION for logic but the original text X-FOO is preserved on rewrite.

quote: The parameter value can only be "THISANDFUTURE" to indicate a range defined by the recurrence identifier and all subsequent instances.
test: RECURRENCE-ID;RANGE=THISANDFUTURE:19980401T133000Z applies the override to that instance and every later instance of the same UID.

quote: The value "THISANDPRIOR" is deprecated by this revision of iCalendar and MUST NOT be generated by applications.
test: No generated output contains RANGE=THISANDPRIOR; a parsed RANGE=THISANDPRIOR is tolerated without crashing and reported as unsupported.

quote: If the parameter is not specified on an allowable property, then the default is START.
test: TRIGGER:-PT15M fires 15 minutes before DTSTART; TRIGGER;RELATED=END:PT0S fires at the event end.

quote: If not specified on a property that allows this parameter, the default value is REQ-PARTICIPANT.
test: An ATTENDEE without ROLE is reported with role REQ-PARTICIPANT.

quote: If not specified on a property that allows this parameter, the default value is FALSE.
test: An ATTENDEE without RSVP is reported with rsvp FALSE.

quote: The parameter value MUST be a mailto URI as defined in [RFC2368].
test: ORGANIZER;SENT-BY="mailto:s@x":mailto:o@x round-trips unchanged through an edit of SUMMARY.

quote: This parameter MUST be specified on the "DTSTART", "DTEND", "DUE", "EXDATE", and "RDATE" properties when either a DATE-TIME or TIME value type is specified and when the value is neither a UTC or a "floating" time.
test: A zoned event is generated as DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240101T100000 with the TZID also on DTEND and on every EXDATE/RDATE of that event.

quote: The value of the "TZID" property parameter will be equal to the value of the "TZID" property for the matching time zone definition.
test: EXDATE;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240102T100000 excludes the instance starting at 10:00 Berlin time (09:00Z); an EXDATE in UTC for the same instant also matches.

quote: An individual "VTIMEZONE" calendar component MUST be specified for each unique "TZID" parameter value specified in the iCalendar object.
test: Generating an event with TZID=Europe/Berlin embeds exactly one VTIMEZONE with TZID:Europe/Berlin; two events with different TZIDs embed two.

quote: The "TZID" property parameter MUST NOT be applied to DATE properties and DATE-TIME or TIME properties whose time values are specified in UTC.
test: DTSTART;VALUE=DATE;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240101 and DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240101T100000Z are both rejected (the earlier matrix wrongly mentioned only the UTC case).

quote: The use of local time in a DATE-TIME or TIME value without the "TZID" property parameter is to be interpreted as floating time, regardless of the existence of "VTIMEZONE" calendar components in the iCalendar object.
test: DTSTART:20240101T100000 in a file that also defines a VTIMEZONE is still floating and resolves in the viewer's local zone.

quote: The presence of the SOLIDUS character as a prefix, indicates that this "TZID" represents an unique ID in a globally defined time zone registry (when such registry is defined).
test: TZID=/example.org/America/New_York is accepted as an opaque label and matched only against a VTIMEZONE with the identical TZID text; it is not assumed to be an IANA name.

quote: Failure to include and follow VTIMEZONE definitions in iCalendar objects may lead to inconsistent understanding of the local time at any given location.
test: A TZID without a VTIMEZONE in the file is resolved by a documented fallback (e.g. system tz database) or reported as an error; the chosen behaviour is deterministic and tested.

quote: The property values MUST be of a single value type.
test: RDATE;VALUE=DATE:20240101,20240102 is accepted; RDATE:20240101,20240102T100000 is rejected.

quote: However, if the property's default value type is overridden by some other allowable value type, then this parameter MUST be specified.
test: An all-day event is generated as DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20240105; a bare DTSTART:20240105 is rejected (or flagged) because the default type is DATE-TIME.

quote: If the value type of a property is one of the alternate valid types, then it MUST be explicitly specified with the "VALUE" parameter.
test: EXDATE for an all-day series is generated as EXDATE;VALUE=DATE:20240102 and RDATE with periods as RDATE;VALUE=PERIOD:...

quote: Property values with this value type MUST also include the inline encoding parameter sequence of ";ENCODING=BASE64".
test: VALUE=BINARY without ENCODING=BASE64 is an error and BINARY values are not backslash-unescaped.

quote: These values are case-insensitive text.
test: TRUE, true and True parse as true; FALSE as false; "1" is rejected; the generator writes uppercase TRUE/FALSE.

quote: email transport address for a calendar user, the value MUST be a mailto URI, as defined by [RFC2368].
test: ATTENDEE:mailto:a@b.c is accepted; ATTENDEE:a@b.c is rejected (or accepted with a warning in lenient mode); the generator always prefixes mailto:.

quote: There are no separator characters between the year, month, and day component text.
test: 20240229 is a valid DATE; 2024-02-29, 240229 and 20230229 are rejected.

quote: The form of date and time with UTC offset MUST NOT be used.
test: DTSTART:19980119T230000-0800 is a parse error.

quote: DATE-TIME values of this type are said to be "floating" and are not bound to any time zone in particular.
test: DTSTART:20240101T100000 is stored as floating and an injected local zone of Europe/Berlin vs America/New_York gives 10:00 local in both.

quote: SHOULD interpret the value as being fixed to whatever time zone the "ATTENDEE" is in at any given moment.
test: Expanding a floating event with an injected zone Asia/Tokyo yields instants at 10:00 Tokyo time, not at a stored offset.

quote: either UTC time or local time with time zone reference MUST be specified.
test: new_event with an explicit timezone generates TZID or Z form, never a bare local time; floating output only when the caller asks for floating.

quote: The date with UTC time, or absolute time, is identified by a LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Z suffix character, the UTC designator, appended to the time value.
test: DTSTART:20240101T100000Z is the instant 2024-01-01T10:00:00Z; a lowercase z is rejected or normalised.

quote: The "TZID" property parameter MUST NOT be applied to DATE-TIME properties whose time values are specified in UTC.
test: DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240101T100000Z is a parse error and is never generated.

quote: the DATE-TIME value refers to the first occurrence of the referenced time.
test: TZID=Europe/Berlin:20241027T023000 (repeated 02:00-03:00 on DST end) resolves to the first occurrence, offset +02:00, i.e. 2024-10-27T00:30:00Z.

quote: the DATE-TIME value is interpreted using the UTC offset before the gap in local times.
test: TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240331T023000 (nonexistent) is interpreted with offset +01:00, i.e. 2024-03-31T01:30:00Z (03:30 CEST), matching the RFC's America/New_York:20070311T023000 -> 03:30 EDT example.

quote: A time value MUST only specify the second 60 when specifying a positive leap second.
test: 19970630T235960Z parses (second 60 treated as 59 when leap seconds are unsupported); 20240101T100060Z is rejected; T240000 is rejected because hour is 00-23.

quote: Implementations that do not support leap seconds SHOULD interpret the second 60 as equivalent to the second 59.
this value type doesn't support the "Y" and "M" designators to specify durations in terms of years and months.
test: P15DT5H0M20S and -PT15M parse; P1M and P1Y are rejected.

quote: "P" (dur-date / dur-time / dur-week)
test: P7W parses as 7 weeks; P1W2D and P1WT1H are rejected because dur-week is an alternative to dur-date/dur-time, not combinable.

quote: Leap seconds MUST NOT be considered when computing an exact duration.
test: Adding PT24H to 2016-12-31T00:00:00Z gives 2017-01-01T00:00:00Z (86400 s, no leap second).

quote: When computing an exact duration, the greatest order time components MUST be added first, that is, the number of days MUST be added first, followed by the number of hours, number of minutes, and number of seconds.
test: Adding P1DT2H to 2024-03-30T12:00 Europe/Berlin adds the day first (2024-03-31T12:00 local, wall-clock) and then 2 exact hours, giving 14:00 CEST (12:00Z).

quote: The duration of a week or a day depends on its position in the calendar.
test: A P1D event starting 2024-03-30T10:00 Europe/Berlin ends 2024-03-31T10:00 local (23 exact hours); PT24H ends 11:00 local.

quote: The valid range for "integer" is -2147483648 to 2147483647.
test: SEQUENCE:2147483647 parses; SEQUENCE:2147483648 is rejected; PRIORITY:+5 parses as 5.

quote: If the sign is not specified, then the value is assumed to be positive.
test: REPEAT:4 and REPEAT:+4 both parse to 4.

quote: The start of the period MUST be before the end of the period.
test: RDATE;VALUE=PERIOD:19970101T180000Z/19970102T070000Z parses; the same with start after end is rejected.

quote: Second, a period of time can also be defined by a start and a positive duration of time.
test: 19970101T180000Z/PT5H30M parses as a 5.5 hour period; 19970101T180000Z/-PT1H is rejected.

quote: This rule part MUST be specified in the recurrence rule.
test: RRULE:COUNT=3 (no FREQ) is a parse error.

quote: Individual rule parts MUST only be specified once.
test: RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;FREQ=WEEKLY and RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=2;COUNT=3 are parse errors.

quote: Compliant applications MUST accept rule parts ordered in any sequence, but to ensure backward compatibility with applications that pre-date this revision of iCalendar the FREQ rule part MUST be the first rule part specified in a RECUR value.
test: COUNT=3;FREQ=DAILY parses; a generated or edited RRULE always starts with FREQ= (e.g. FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO;COUNT=3).

quote: The value of the UNTIL rule part MUST have the same value type as the "DTSTART" property.
test: DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20240101 with UNTIL=20240110T000000Z is rejected; with UNTIL=20240110 is accepted.

quote: if the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with local time, then the UNTIL rule part MUST also be specified as a date with local time.
test: Floating DTSTART:20240101T100000 with UNTIL=20240110T100000 is accepted; UNTIL=20240110T100000Z is rejected.

quote: If the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with UTC time or a date with local time and time zone reference, then the UNTIL rule part MUST be specified as a date with UTC time.
test: DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240101T100000 with UNTIL=20240110T090000Z is accepted; UNTIL=20240110T100000 (no Z) is rejected; ending a series generates a Z value.

quote: In the case of the "STANDARD" and "DAYLIGHT" sub-components the UNTIL rule part MUST always be specified as a date with UTC time.
test: A generated VTIMEZONE observance with an end date uses UNTIL=...Z (e.g. UNTIL=20061029T060000Z); a non-Z UNTIL in a STANDARD block is rejected.

quote: The UNTIL rule part defines a DATE or DATE-TIME value that bounds the recurrence rule in an inclusive manner.
test: DAILY from 2024-01-01T10:00Z with UNTIL=20240103T100000Z yields exactly Jan 1, 2 and 3 (the UNTIL instant is included).

quote: If specified as a DATE-TIME value, then it MUST be specified in a UTC time format.
test: Ending a Europe/Berlin 10:00 series so that the last instance is Jan 10 writes UNTIL=20240110T090000Z (converted to UTC, at or after the last wanted start).

quote: but they MUST NOT occur in the same 'recur'.
test: FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3;UNTIL=20240110T000000Z is rejected; editing a COUNT series to end it replaces COUNT with UNTIL (never both). This corrects the earlier note that called it SHOULD NOT.

quote: The COUNT rule part defines the number of occurrences at which to range-bound the recurrence.
test: DTSTART:20240101T100000Z with FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3 yields exactly three instances.

quote: The "DTSTART" property value always counts as the first occurrence.
test: FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3 from Jan 1 yields Jan 1, 2, 3 (DTSTART is occurrence 1, so not Jan 2-4).

quote: The INTERVAL rule part contains a positive integer representing at which intervals the recurrence rule repeats.
test: INTERVAL=0 is rejected; FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=10;INTERVAL=2 yields every other day; absent INTERVAL means 1.

quote: significant when a WEEKLY "RRULE" has an interval greater than 1, and a BYDAY rule part is specified.
test: RFC example: DTSTART;TZID=America/New_York:19970805T090000, FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;COUNT=4;BYDAY=TU,SU;WKST=MO yields Aug 5,10,19,24; with WKST=SU yields Aug 5,17,19,31.

quote: This is also significant when in a YEARLY "RRULE" when a BYWEEKNO rule part is specified. The default value is MO.
test: A WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=TU,SU rule without WKST expands exactly like the same rule with WKST=MO.

quote: The BYSECOND, BYMINUTE and BYHOUR rule parts MUST NOT be specified when the associated "DTSTART" property has a DATE value type.
test: An all-day event with FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9 is rejected by the generator/validator.

quote: These rule parts MUST be ignored in RECUR value that violate the above requirement (e.g., generated by applications that pre-date this revision of iCalendar).
test: When expanding an existing all-day DAILY;BYHOUR=9 rule the BYHOUR part is ignored and one all-day instance per day is produced.

quote: The BYDAY rule part MUST NOT be specified with a numeric value when the FREQ rule part is not set to MONTHLY or YEARLY.
test: FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=1MO is rejected; FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR (last Friday) is accepted.

quote: Furthermore, the BYDAY rule part MUST NOT be specified with a numeric value with the FREQ rule part set to YEARLY when the BYWEEKNO rule part is specified.
test: FREQ=YEARLY;BYWEEKNO=20;BYDAY=1MO is rejected; FREQ=YEARLY;BYWEEKNO=20;BYDAY=MO is accepted.

quote: The BYMONTHDAY rule part MUST NOT be specified when the FREQ rule part is set to WEEKLY.
test: FREQ=WEEKLY;BYMONTHDAY=1 is rejected; FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=-1 (last day of month) is accepted.

quote: The BYYEARDAY rule part MUST NOT be specified when the FREQ rule part is set to DAILY, WEEKLY, or MONTHLY.
test: FREQ=DAILY;BYYEARDAY=1 is rejected; FREQ=YEARLY;BYYEARDAY=-1 yields December 31 each year.

quote: This rule part MUST NOT be used when the FREQ rule part is set to anything other than YEARLY.
test: FREQ=MONTHLY;BYWEEKNO=1 is rejected; FREQ=YEARLY;BYWEEKNO=20;BYDAY=MO is accepted.

quote: It MUST only be used in conjunction with another BYxxx rule part.
test: FREQ=MONTHLY;BYSETPOS=1 is rejected; FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYSETPOS=-1 yields the last weekday of each month.

quote: Such recurrence instances MUST be ignored and MUST NOT be counted as part of the recurrence set.
test: DTSTART 2007-01-15 with FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=15,30;COUNT=5 yields Jan 15,30, Feb 15, Mar 15,30 (Feb 30 skipped and not counted); MONTHLY from Jan 31 COUNT=3 yields Jan 31, Mar 31, May 31. The same paragraph also lists nonexistent local times, which conflicts with the later paragraph; see the gap policy row.

quote: If the computed local start time of a recurrence instance does not exist, or occurs more than once, for the specified time zone, the time of the recurrence instance is interpreted in the same manner as an explicit DATE-TIME value describing that date and time, as specified in Section 3.3.5.
test: DAILY 02:30 Europe/Berlin across 2024-03-31 yields an instance at 01:30Z (03:30 CEST) using the offset before the gap, and on 2024-10-27 the first (CEST) occurrence. The RFC is self-contradictory here (an earlier paragraph says nonexistent local times are ignored and not counted); we follow this later, more specific paragraph and counts include these instances.

quote: the BYxxx rule parts are applied to the current set of evaluated occurrences in the following order: BYMONTH, BYWEEKNO, BYYEARDAY, BYMONTHDAY, BYDAY, BYHOUR, BYMINUTE, BYSECOND and BYSETPOS; then COUNT and UNTIL are evaluated.
test: FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=TU,WE;BYSETPOS=2 yields the 2nd Tuesday-or-Wednesday of each month (BYSETPOS applied after BYDAY, COUNT after BYSETPOS).

quote: Valid values are 1 to 31 or -31 to -1.
test: BYMONTHDAY=0 and BYMONTHDAY=32 are rejected; -31 and 31 are accepted.

quote: The BYYEARDAY rule part specifies a COMMA-separated list of days of the year. Valid values are 1 to 366 or -366 to -1.
test: BYYEARDAY=0 and BYYEARDAY=367 are rejected; -366 and 366 are accepted.

quote: Valid values are 1 to 53 or -53 to -1.
test: BYWEEKNO=54 and BYWEEKNO=0 are rejected; 53 and -53 are accepted.

quote: Valid values are 1 to 12.
test: BYMONTH=0 and BYMONTH=13 are rejected; 1 and 12 are accepted.

quote: Valid values are 0 to 60.
test: BYSECOND=61 is rejected; BYSECOND=0 and 60 are accepted; BYMINUTE>59 and BYHOUR>23 are rejected.

quote: The term "N/A" means that the corresponding BYxxx rule part MUST NOT be used with the corresponding FREQ value.
test: Every N/A cell of the BYxxx table (BYWEEKNO non-YEARLY, BYYEARDAY DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY, BYMONTHDAY WEEKLY) is rejected by a table-driven validator test.

quote: |BYMONTH   |Limit   |Limit   |Limit  |Limit  |Limit |Limit  |Expand|
test: FREQ=DAILY;BYMONTH=1 limits to days in January; FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=1,3 expands to two instances per year.

quote: |BYWEEKNO  |N/A     |N/A     |N/A    |N/A    |N/A   |N/A    |Expand|
test: FREQ=YEARLY;BYWEEKNO=20;BYDAY=MO expands to Mondays of ISO week 20 (week 1 has at least four days in the year, WKST-aligned); other FREQs are rejected.

quote: |BYYEARDAY |Limit   |Limit   |Limit  |N/A    |N/A   |N/A    |Expand|
test: HOURLY;BYYEARDAY=1 limits to Jan 1; YEARLY;BYYEARDAY=1,100,200 expands; DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY with BYYEARDAY are rejected.

quote: |BYMONTHDAY|Limit   |Limit   |Limit  |Limit  |N/A   |Expand |Expand|
test: DAILY;BYMONTHDAY=1 limits to first-of-month days; MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=1,15 expands; WEEKLY with BYMONTHDAY is rejected.

quote: Note 1: Limit if BYMONTHDAY is present; otherwise, special expand for MONTHLY.
test: MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO;BYMONTHDAY=13 limits to Mondays that are the 13th; MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO expands to all Mondays of the month; YEARLY;BYDAY=MO without BYMONTH/BYWEEKNO expands to every Monday of the year (Note 2).

quote: BYxxx rule parts for a period of time that is the same or greater than the frequency generally reduce or limit the number of occurrences of the recurrence generated.
test: FREQ=DAILY;BYMONTH=1 reduces all days to the days in January.

quote: BYxxx rule parts for a period of time less than the frequency generally increase or expand the number of occurrences of the recurrence.
test: FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=1,2 yields two instances per year.

quote: Information, not contained in the rule, necessary to determine the various recurrence instance start time and dates are derived from the Start Time ("DTSTART") component attribute.
test: DTSTART 1997-01-05T08:30:00 with FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=1 yields January 5 at 08:30:00 each year (day, time and seconds from DTSTART).

quote: An intentional formatted text line break MUST only be included in a "TEXT" property value by representing the line break with the character sequence of BACKSLASH, followed by a LATIN SMALL LETTER N or a LATIN CAPITAL LETTER N, that is "\n" or "\N".
test: A DESCRIPTION containing a LF is written as two characters backslash-n; both \n and \N decode to LF on parse; no raw LF/CR appears in a content line.

quote: A BACKSLASH character in a "TEXT" property value MUST be escaped with another BACKSLASH character.
test: Text a\b is generated as a\\b and a\\b decodes to a\b (single backslash).

quote: A COMMA character in a "TEXT" property value MUST be escaped with a BACKSLASH character.
test: LOCATION "Room 1, Bldg 2" is generated as Room 1\, Bldg 2 and parsed back unchanged.

quote: A SEMICOLON character in a "TEXT" property value MUST be escaped with a BACKSLASH character.
test: SUMMARY "a;b" is generated as a\;b and parsed back unchanged.

quote: However, a COLON character in a "TEXT" property value SHALL NOT be escaped with a BACKSLASH character.
test: SUMMARY "Meeting: planning" is generated without a backslash before the colon; the parser leniently reads an incoming backslash-colon as a colon.

quote: consists of a two-digit, 24-hour of the day (i.e., values 00-23),
test: Time 083000 and 133000Z parse; 240000 and 2530 are rejected.

quote: Fractions of a second are not supported by this format.
test: DTSTART:20240101T100000.5Z is rejected.

quote: The form of time with UTC offset MUST NOT be used.
test: A TIME value 230000-0800 is rejected.

quote: Property values with this value type MUST follow the generic URI syntax defined in [RFC3986].
test: URL:http://example.com/x is accepted; a URL value containing a space is rejected.

quote: When a property parameter value is a URI value type, the URI MUST be specified as a quoted-string value.
test: SENT-BY, DIR, DELEGATED-FROM/TO, MEMBER and ALTREP values are always emitted inside DQUOTEs.

quote: The PLUS SIGN character MUST be specified for positive UTC offsets (i.e., ahead of UTC).
test: TZOFFSETTO:+0100 parses and is generated with the plus sign; TZOFFSETTO:0100 is rejected.

quote: The HYPHEN-MINUS character MUST be specified for negative UTC offsets (i.e., behind of UTC).
test: TZOFFSETFROM:-0500 parses as minus five hours.

quote: The value of "-0000" and "-000000" are not allowed.
test: -0000 and -000000 are rejected; +0000 is accepted and generated for UTC offsets of zero.

quote: The time-second, if present, MUST NOT be 60; if absent, it defaults to zero.
test: +010060 is rejected; +0530 and +053000 are equal.

quote: The first line and last line of the iCalendar object MUST contain a pair of iCalendar object delimiter strings.
test: Generated files start with BEGIN:VCALENDAR and end with END:VCALENDAR + CRLF; a file missing END:VCALENDAR is a parse error.

quote: However, multiple iCalendar objects can be sequentially grouped together in an iCalendar stream.
test: A file with two sequential VCALENDAR objects yields two objects/all their events.

quote: This memo imposes no ordering of properties within an iCalendar object.
test: A VEVENT with DTEND before DTSTART, or RRULE before DTSTART, parses identically to the canonical order, and edits preserve the original property order.

quote: An iCalendar object MUST include the "PRODID" and "VERSION" calendar properties.
test: Generated calendars contain VERSION:2.0 and a PRODID; a VCALENDAR without VERSION is reported (error or lenient warning).

quote: In addition, it MUST include at least one calendar component.
test: A VCALENDAR with only VERSION and PRODID is reported as invalid; deleting the last component from a generated file is not done by rewriting an empty VCALENDAR.

quote: Applications MUST ignore x-comp and iana-comp values they don't recognize.
test: A VCALENDAR containing BEGIN:X-FOO ... END:X-FOO next to a VEVENT parses the VEVENT without error.

quote: SHOULD NOT silently drop any components as that can lead to user data loss.
test: Editing one VEVENT in a file that also contains a VTODO, VJOURNAL and an X- component rewrites the file with all of those components still present.

quote: They SHOULD be specified after the "BEGIN:VCALENDAR" delimiter string and prior to any calendar component.
test: Generated output places VERSION, PRODID (and CALSCALE) between BEGIN:VCALENDAR and the first BEGIN:VEVENT/VTIMEZONE.

quote: The default value is "GREGORIAN".
test: A calendar without CALSCALE is treated as Gregorian; a CALSCALE other than GREGORIAN is reported as unsupported.

quote: If this property is not present in the iCalendar object, then a scheduling transaction MUST NOT be assumed.
test: A file without METHOD is handled as a plain calendar snapshot, never as an invitation request or reply.

quote: The property MUST be specified once in an iCalendar object.
test: Two PRODID lines in one VCALENDAR are reported; the generator emits exactly one.

quote: This property MUST be specified once in an iCalendar object.
test: Two VERSION lines are reported; the generator emits exactly one.

quote: A value of "2.0" corresponds to this memo.
test: Generated calendars contain exactly VERSION:2.0.

quote: The property MUST be specified in the "VEVENT", "VTODO", "VJOURNAL", or "VFREEBUSY" calendar components.
test: A VEVENT without UID is rejected (or flagged); a duplicate UID property inside one VEVENT is an error; the generator always writes exactly one UID.

quote: This property MUST be included in the "VEVENT", "VTODO", "VJOURNAL", or "VFREEBUSY" calendar components.
test: A VEVENT without DTSTAMP is flagged; the generator writes DTSTAMP from the injected clock and updates it when an event is edited.

quote: This property is also REQUIRED in "VEVENT" calendar components contained in iCalendar objects that don't specify the "METHOD" property.
test: A VEVENT without DTSTART in a file without METHOD is reported; with METHOD:REQUEST it is tolerated (DTSTART is optional there).

quote: This property is REQUIRED in all types of recurring calendar components that specify the "RRULE" property.
test: A VEVENT with RRULE but no DTSTART is rejected and produces no instances.

quote: The default value type is DATE-TIME. The time value MUST be one of the forms defined for the DATE-TIME value type.
test: DTSTART:20240105T100000Z is DATE-TIME; DTSTART:20240105 without VALUE=DATE is flagged (lenient parsers may read it as DATE with a warning).

quote: MUST NOT occur in the same 'eventprop'.
test: A VEVENT with both DTEND and DURATION is rejected; editing the end of an event that uses DURATION replaces DURATION by DTEND (or vice versa), never leaving both.

quote: class / created / description / geo /
test: Per the grammar group headed 'OPTIONAL, but MUST NOT occur more than once' (CLASS, CREATED, DESCRIPTION, GEO, LAST-MODIFIED, LOCATION, ORGANIZER, PRIORITY, SEQUENCE, STATUS, SUMMARY, TRANSP, URL, RECURRENCE-ID), two SUMMARY lines in one VEVENT are reported and the editor writes exactly one.

quote: attach / attendee / categories / comment /
test: A VEVENT with two EXDATE lines and two RDATE lines uses the union of all their values when expanding.

quote: but SHOULD NOT occur more than once.
test: The generator never emits a second RRULE; the parser accepts a file with two RRULEs without crashing (SHOULD NOT, not MUST NOT).

quote: but it SHOULD NOT be specified more than once. The recurrence set generated with multiple "RRULE" properties is undefined.
test: Expanding a VEVENT with two RRULEs follows one documented behaviour (e.g. union or first rule only) and reports a warning.

quote: If such a "VEVENT" has a "DTEND" property, it MUST be specified as a DATE value also.
test: DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20240105 with DTEND:20240106T100000Z is rejected; DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20240106 is accepted.

quote: The "DTEND" property for a "VEVENT" calendar component specifies the non-inclusive end of the event.
test: An event DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20070628 / DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20070709 spans June 28 through July 8 inclusive; a one-day all-day event is generated with DTEND = DTSTART + 1 day.

quote: For cases where a "VEVENT" calendar component specifies a "DTSTART" property with a DATE value type but no "DTEND" nor "DURATION" property, the event's duration is taken to be one day.
test: DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20240105 with no DTEND/DURATION occupies only Jan 5 (exclusive end Jan 6).

quote: For cases where a "VEVENT" calendar component specifies a "DTSTART" property with a DATE-TIME value type but no "DTEND" property, the event ends on the same calendar date and time of day specified by the "DTSTART" property.
test: DTSTART:20240105T100000Z with no DTEND is a zero-length event (end == start); with DURATION:PT1H (allowed by the grammar) the end is start + 1h.

quote: The value type of this property MUST be the same as the "DTSTART" property, and its value MUST be later in time than the value of the "DTSTART" property.
test: DTEND before or equal to DTSTART is rejected by the validator/editor; a DATE DTSTART with a DATE-TIME DTEND is rejected.

quote: Furthermore, this property MUST be specified as a date with local time if and only if the "DTSTART" property is also specified as a date with local time.
test: Floating DTSTART:20240105T100000 with DTEND:20240105T110000Z is rejected; floating DTEND with a UTC DTSTART is rejected; TZID DTSTART with UTC DTEND is allowed (both non-floating).

quote: This property specifies a positive duration of time.
test: A VEVENT with DURATION:-PT1H is rejected while a VALARM TRIGGER:-PT15M (a different property) is accepted.

quote: When the "DURATION" property relates to a "DTSTART" property that is specified as a DATE value, then the "DURATION" property MUST be specified as a "dur-day" or "dur-week" value.
test: DTSTART;VALUE=DATE with DURATION:PT1H is rejected; DURATION:P2D and P1W are accepted.

quote: If not specified in a component that allows this property, the default value is PUBLIC.
test: A VEVENT without CLASS reports class PUBLIC.

quote: Applications MUST treat x-name and iana-token values they don't recognize the same way as they would the PRIVATE value.
test: CLASS:X-FOO is handled as PRIVATE (event not exposed) while the original text is preserved on rewrite.

quote: statvalue-event = "TENTATIVE"
test: VEVENT STATUS accepts TENTATIVE, CONFIRMED and CANCELLED only; STATUS:COMPLETED (a VTODO value) on a VEVENT is rejected by the generator.

quote: This property can be specified once in "VEVENT", "VTODO", or "VJOURNAL" calendar components.
test: Setting STATUS:CANCELLED on an event that already has STATUS replaces it instead of adding a second line.

quote: Default value is OPAQUE
test: A VEVENT without TRANSP is OPAQUE; only OPAQUE and TRANSPARENT are valid values.

quote: The value MUST be specified in the UTC time format.
test: DTSTAMP:20240101T100000 (no Z) is flagged; the generator writes DTSTAMP from the injected clock as ...Z.

quote: The value MUST be specified as a date with UTC time.
test: CREATED:19960329T133000Z is accepted; a CREATED without Z is flagged; CREATED is not changed by edits.

quote: The property value MUST be specified in the UTC time format.
test: An edit sets LAST-MODIFIED to the injected clock time in ...Z form (if the property is maintained).

quote: When a calendar component is created, its sequence number is 0.
test: A newly created event has SEQUENCE:0 (or none, treated as 0).

quote: It is monotonically incremented by the "Organizer's" CUA each time the "Organizer" makes a significant revision to the calendar component.
test: Editing the start time or location of an event we organise increments SEQUENCE by 1 (0 -> 1); an unrelated edit leaves it unchanged; SEQUENCE never decreases.

quote: Recurrence instances of a recurring component MAY have different sequence numbers.
test: An override VEVENT with SEQUENCE:2 next to a master with SEQUENCE:0 is accepted and the two are not forced equal.

quote: The "UID" itself MUST be a globally unique identifier. The generator of the identifier MUST guarantee that the identifier is unique.
test: Two generated events have different UIDs (injected random source, UUID plus @host part); editing an event keeps its UID.

quote: Implementations MUST be able to receive and persist values of at least 255 octets for this property, but they MUST NOT truncate values in the middle of a UTF-8 multi-octet sequence.
test: A 300-octet UID (including a multi-byte character) is parsed, edited and written back unchanged, never truncated or split.

quote: This property MUST NOT be specified in an iCalendar object when publishing the calendar information (e.g., NOT in an iCalendar object that specifies the publication of a calendar user's busy time, event, to-do, or journal).
test: new_event without invitees generates no ATTENDEE or ORGANIZER line (a single-user calendar entry is not group-scheduled).

quote: They MUST NOT be specified in an "ATTENDEE" property in a "VFREEBUSY" or "VALARM" calendar component.
test: Correction: the MUST NOT applies to the ATTENDEE parameters (CN, ROLE, PARTSTAT, RSVP, CUTYPE, MEMBER, DELEGATED-*, SENT-BY, DIR), not to ATTENDEE itself. An EMAIL VALARM has a bare ATTENDEE:mailto:x line without those parameters.

quote: The property is specified within an "EMAIL" category of the "VALARM" calendar component to specify an email address that is to receive the email type of iCalendar alarm.
test: An EMAIL VALARM with ATTENDEE:mailto:john@example.com parses without error (the earlier matrix summary wrongly implied ATTENDEE is forbidden in VALARM).

quote: A recipient delegated a request MUST inherit the "RSVP" and "ROLE" values from the attendee that delegated the request to them.
test: Not applicable: this server never creates delegations.
reason: mcp-khal has no delegation workflow (respond_to_event only changes PARTSTAT of the user's own ATTENDEE line).

quote: The non-standard parameters may also be specified on this property.
test: ORGANIZER;CN="John Smith";SENT-BY="mailto:j@x";X-FOO=1:mailto:o@x is preserved byte-equivalent (parameters and order) when another property of the event is edited.

quote: The "VALARM" calendar component MUST include the "ACTION" and "TRIGGER" properties.
test: A VALARM without TRIGGER (or without ACTION) is reported as invalid; generated alarms always have both.

quote: When the action is "AUDIO", the alarm can also include one and only one "ATTACH" property, which MUST point to a sound resource, which is rendered when the alarm is triggered.
test: An AUDIO alarm with zero or one ATTACH parses; two ATTACH lines are flagged.

quote: When the action is "DISPLAY", the alarm MUST also include a "DESCRIPTION" property, which contains the text to be displayed when the alarm is triggered.
test: ACTION:DISPLAY without DESCRIPTION is flagged; generated display alarms always include DESCRIPTION.

quote: When the action is "EMAIL", the alarm MUST include a "DESCRIPTION" property, which contains the text to be used as the message body, a "SUMMARY" property, which contains the text to be used as the message subject, and one or more "ATTENDEE" properties, which contain the email address of attendees to receive the message.
test: An EMAIL alarm missing DESCRIPTION, SUMMARY or ATTENDEE is flagged; one with all three parses.

quote: Both of these properties MUST be present in order to specify a repeating alarm.
test: REPEAT:2 with DURATION:PT5M fires three times in total (initial plus 2 repetitions at 5-minute intervals).

quote: If one of these two properties is absent, then the alarm will not repeat beyond the initial trigger.
test: A VALARM with REPEAT:2 but no DURATION (or the reverse) fires exactly once (the grammar says if one occurs so MUST the other, so the generator never writes only one).

quote: but if one occurs, so MUST the other.
test: Generating an alarm with only DURATION or only REPEAT is rejected by the builder.

quote: If the alarm triggers more than once, then this property MUST be specified along with the "DURATION" property.
test: REPEAT:4;DURATION:PT5M means 4 additional triggers after the initial one (5 total).

quote: Applications MUST ignore alarms with x-name and iana-token values they don't recognize.
test: ACTION:X-FOO alarms are skipped without an error and are retained in the file when the event is edited.

quote: This property MUST be specified once in a "VALARM" calendar component.
test: A VALARM with two ACTION lines is flagged; generated alarms have exactly one.

quote: The default value type is DURATION, specifying a relative time for the trigger of the alarm.
test: TRIGGER:-PT15M on an event starting 10:00Z fires at 09:45Z; the generator writes a negative DURATION for a reminder before the start.

quote: An alarm with a negative duration is triggered before the associated start or end of the event or to-do.
test: TRIGGER;RELATED=END:PT5M fires five minutes after the end; TRIGGER;RELATED=END:-PT5M fires five minutes before the end.

quote: If a value type of DATE-TIME is specified, then the property value MUST be specified in the UTC time format.
test: TRIGGER;VALUE=DATE-TIME:19980101T050000Z is accepted; the same without Z is rejected.

quote: The trigger relationship property parameter MUST only be specified when the value type is "DURATION".
test: TRIGGER;VALUE=DATE-TIME;RELATED=END:19980101T050000Z is rejected.

quote: Alarms specified in an event or to-do that is defined in terms of a DATE value type will be triggered relative to 00:00:00 of the user's configured time zone on the specified date, or relative to 00:00:00 UTC on the specified date if no configured time zone can be found for the user.
test: An all-day event on 1998-02-05 with TRIGGER:-PT15M fires 1998-02-04T23:45 in the injected user zone (e.g. America/New_York), or 23:45Z when no zone is configured.

quote: If the trigger is set relative to START, then the "DTSTART" property MUST be present in the associated "VEVENT" or "VTODO" calendar component.
test: A VEVENT without DTSTART containing a start-relative alarm is flagged; the generator never adds an alarm to an event lacking DTSTART.

quote: If an alarm is specified for an event with the trigger set relative to the END, then the "DTEND" property or the "DTSTART" and "DURATION " properties MUST be present in the associated "VEVENT" calendar component.
test: TRIGGER;RELATED=END on an event with only DTSTART (zero length) is flagged; with DTEND or DURATION it is accepted.

quote: If an absolute trigger is specified on an alarm for a recurring event or to-do, then the alarm will only trigger for the specified absolute DATE-TIME, along with any specified repeating instances.
test: A recurring daily event with TRIGGER;VALUE=DATE-TIME:19980101T050000Z produces one alarm at that instant, not one per occurrence.

quote: The "VALARM" calendar component MUST only appear within either a "VEVENT" or "VTODO" calendar component.
test: A VALARM at VCALENDAR level or nested inside another VALARM is flagged; generated alarms are children of the VEVENT only.

quote: One reasonable policy is to always ignore alarm components that the calendar user has not set herself, or at least ask for confirmation in such a case.
test: Not implemented: alarms come from the user's own calendar files and are shown as stored.
reason: The RFC only gives this as a note; mcp-khal reads only the user's own calendar directories, so no import path from untrusted sources exists.

quote: The "VTIMEZONE" calendar component MUST include the "TZID" property and at least one definition of a "STANDARD" or "DAYLIGHT" sub-component.
test: An empty VTIMEZONE or one without TZID is rejected; a generated VTIMEZONE has TZID and at least one STANDARD/DAYLIGHT.

quote: The "STANDARD" or "DAYLIGHT" sub-component MUST include the "DTSTART", "TZOFFSETFROM", and "TZOFFSETTO" properties.
test: A STANDARD block missing TZOFFSETTO is rejected; generated observances carry all three.

quote: "DTSTART" in this usage MUST be specified as a date with a local time value.
test: STANDARD DTSTART:19671029T020000 is accepted; DTSTART with Z or with TZID inside a STANDARD block is rejected.

quote: MUST be specified as a date with local time without the "TZID" property parameter.
test: A generated observance DTSTART has no TZID parameter.

quote: In addition, a "VTIMEZONE" calendar component, referred to by a recurring calendar component, MUST provide valid time zone information for all recurrence instances.
test: A generated VTIMEZONE for an unbounded weekly Europe/Berlin event includes recurring DST rules (RRULE-based observances) so every future instance resolves, not just the first year.

quote: In this situation, each "VTIMEZONE" MUST represent a unique time zone definition.
test: Merging two events that both use Europe/Berlin into one file yields a single VTIMEZONE TZID:Europe/Berlin.

quote: The offset to apply at any given time is found by locating the observance that has the last onset date and time before the time in question, and using the offset value from that observance.
test: With the RFC America/New_York VTIMEZONE, a local time on 2007-07-01 resolves to -0400 (DAYLIGHT onset 2007-03-11) and on 2007-12-01 to -0500.

quote: The "DTSTART" and the "TZOFFSETFROM" properties MUST be used when generating the onset DATE-TIME values (instances) from the "RRULE".
test: Onset of DAYLIGHT 02:00 local with TZOFFSETFROM -0500 is 07:00Z; of STANDARD 02:00 with TZOFFSETFROM -0400 is 06:00Z.

quote: If observance is known to have an effective end date, the "UNTIL" recurrence rule parameter MUST be used to specify the last valid onset of this observance
test: DAYLIGHT 1967-1973 with UNTIL=19730429T070000Z produces no onset after April 29 1973.

quote: "RDATE" in this usage MUST be specified as a date with local time value, relative to the UTC offset specified in the "TZOFFSETFROM" property.
test: DAYLIGHT RDATE:19750223T020000 with TZOFFSETFROM:-0500 is the instant 1975-02-23T07:00:00Z.

quote: Positive numbers represent time zones east of the prime meridian, or ahead of UTC.
test: TZOFFSETTO:+0100 means local = UTC + 1h; TZOFFSETTO:-0500 means local = UTC - 5h.

quote: The final recurrence set is generated by gathering all of the start DATE-TIME values generated by any of the specified "RRULE" and "RDATE" properties, and then excluding any start DATE-TIME values specified by "EXDATE" properties.
test: Set = (DTSTART + RRULE instances + RDATEs) minus EXDATEs, evaluated in that order for a daily rule with one RDATE and one EXDATE.

quote: However, in such cases, the original "DTSTART" date MUST still be maintained by the calendaring and scheduling system because the original "DTSTART" value has inherent usage dependencies by other properties such as the "RECURRENCE-ID".
test: An EXDATE equal to DTSTART removes the first instance from the expansion, but DTSTART is left unchanged in the file when the event is edited.

quote: The "EXDATE" property can be used to exclude the value specified in "DTSTART".
test: An EXDATE that equals an RDATE removes it from the set; an EXDATE equal to an RRULE instance removes that instance.

quote: Duplicate instances are ignored.
test: An RDATE equal to an RRULE-generated instance (or to DTSTART) yields that instant exactly once.

quote: instances are defined by the union of occurrences defined by both the "RDATE" and "RRULE".
test: WEEKLY rule plus an extra RDATE on a Wednesday gives all weekly instances plus that Wednesday.

quote: The default value type for this property is DATE-TIME. The value type can be set to DATE or PERIOD.
test: RDATE;VALUE=PERIOD:19960403T020000Z/19960403T040000Z adds an instance with a 2 hour duration that overrides the event duration (3.8.5.3 notes a PERIOD RDATE may change one instance's duration).

quote: The default value type for this property is DATE-TIME. The value type can be set to DATE.
test: EXDATE;VALUE=DATE:20240102 excludes the all-day instance of Jan 2; EXDATE;VALUE=PERIOD is rejected.

quote: Value MUST match value type
test: The RFC does not say EXDATE must have DTSTART's type (the quoted rule ties values to the VALUE parameter only); policy: a DATE-TIME EXDATE on a DATE series (or the reverse) matches nothing and is reported, with the behaviour pinned by a test. This corrects the earlier matrix claim of an RFC requirement.

quote: The "DTSTART" property value SHOULD be synchronized with the recurrence rule, if specified.
test: Generating or editing a WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO event adjusts DTSTART to a Monday (or rejects a non-Monday DTSTART); corrects the earlier note which called it MUST.

quote: The recurrence set generated with a "DTSTART" property value not synchronized with the recurrence rule is undefined.
test: DTSTART Monday 2024-01-01 with FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU;COUNT=3 is undefined by the RFC; policy: DTSTART is kept as first instance giving Jan 1, Jan 2, Jan 9, and the behaviour is pinned by a test.

quote: The "DTSTART" property specified within the iCalendar object defines the first instance of the recurrence.
test: Expansion of a daily rule begins at DTSTART, never earlier; an RRULE without BYxxx fills missing parts from DTSTART.

quote: should be specified as a date with local time and time zone reference to make sure all the recurrence instances start at the same local time regardless of time zone changes.
test: A weekly 10:00 Europe/Berlin event generated with TZID stays at 10:00 local across the March and October DST changes (09:00Z in winter, 08:00Z in summer); a UTC DTSTART would drift.

quote: If the duration of the recurring component is specified with the "DTEND" or "DUE" property, then the same exact duration will apply to all the members of the generated recurrence set.
test: A weekly event 10:00-11:00 Europe/Berlin via DTEND is exactly 1 hour long on every instance, including those on DST-change days.

quote: Else, if the duration of the recurring component is specified with the "DURATION" property, then the same nominal duration will apply to all the members of the generated recurrence set and the exact duration of each recurrence instance will depend on its specific start time.
test: A daily event with DURATION:P1D starting 10:00 Europe/Berlin has an exact length of 23 hours on 2024-03-30 and 25 hours on 2024-10-26.

quote: This property MUST have the same value type as the "DTSTART" property contained within the recurring component.
test: A DATE master with a RECURRENCE-ID carrying a DATE-TIME is rejected.

quote: Furthermore, this property MUST be specified as a date with local time if and only if the "DTSTART" property contained within the recurring component is specified as a date with local time.
test: A floating master gets a floating RECURRENCE-ID; a TZID or UTC master gets a RECURRENCE-ID with TZID or Z (never floating).

quote: The property value is the original value of the "DTSTART" property of the recurrence instance.
test: Moving the Jan 3 10:00Z instance to 12:00Z produces an override with RECURRENCE-ID:20240103T100000Z and DTSTART:20240103T120000Z.

quote: The DATE-TIME value is set to the time when the original recurrence instance would occur; meaning that if the intent is to change a Friday meeting to Thursday, the DATE-TIME is still set to the original Friday meeting.
test: Rescheduling a Friday instance to Thursday keeps the Friday date in RECURRENCE-ID and puts the Thursday in DTSTART.

quote: If the value of the "DTSTART" property is a DATE type value, then the value MUST be the calendar date for the recurrence instance.
test: An all-day series override carries RECURRENCE-ID;VALUE=DATE:19960401.

quote: The "RECURRENCE-ID" property allows the reference to an individual instance within the recurrence set.
test: An override VEVENT (same UID, RECURRENCE-ID = original Jan 3 10:00Z) replaces exactly that instance of the master and the other instances remain unchanged.

quote: When the given recurrence instance is rescheduled, all subsequent instances are also rescheduled by the same time difference.
test: RANGE=THISANDFUTURE override moving instance N by +2h moves instances N+1, N+2... by +2h too and changes their duration when the override's duration changes.

quote: Subsequent instances are determined by their "RECURRENCE-ID" value and not their current scheduled start time.
test: After an earlier THISANDFUTURE move, a later override whose RECURRENCE-ID is the original start of an affected instance is still matched by that original value.

quote: the calendar application could simply truncate the unbounded recurring calendar component (i.e., with the "COUNT" or "UNTIL" rule parts), and create two new unbounded recurring calendar components for the future instances.
test: end_event_series on an unbounded rule writes UNTIL (UTC for TZID/Z DTSTART, DATE for DATE DTSTART, floating for floating) just before the chosen instance and removes any COUNT.
An override component (has RECURRENCE-ID) that also carries an RRULE is handled by one documented policy (e.g. RRULE ignored with a warning) pinned by a test.
reason: RFC 5545 has no normative text forbidding or defining RRULE in an override; the earlier matrix claim had no RFC basis, so this is implementation policy only.

test: An override whose RECURRENCE-ID matches no generated instance is neither shown nor deleted when the file is rewritten.
reason: RFC 5545 has no normative text on overrides that match no instance; this is implementation policy to avoid data loss, not an RFC requirement.
